sentences.text: [OP (MAC) Nos.150/2023, 149/2023] The petitioners in these cases are the driver and owner of the vehicle, which met with an accident on 12.09.2018, causing injury to the respondents herein.
OP(MV) No.1638 of 2019 and 1565 of 2019 were filed by the injured.
2. The petitioners herein contended that after the accident, from the next day onwards, the respondents attended the classes, which would show that they had not suffered any serious injury.

Through Ext.P4, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pala, in a common award, relied on the final report filed before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Pala, under Section 279 and 337 of the IPC and Section 146 read with Section 196 of the MV Act against the 1st respondent for rash and negligent driving.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Pala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The Tribunal found that there was no contra evidence adduced and that the 1st petitioner, the driver, was found responsible for the accident and the 2nd petitioner, being the registered owner of the vehicle, 2025:KER:94544 OP (MAC) NO.150 OF 2023 & conn.
was vicariously liable.
Since there was no insurance coverage, the petitioners were directed to compensate the claimants.
4. The Tribunal, in fact, considered the contention of the petitioners herein, and it was found that the injuries were not very serious, and only a consolidated amount was ordered.

The Tribunal also relied on the judgment of this Court in MACA No.455 of 2015 dated 19.02.2016 [Dr. Safia Bee Vs.
National Insurance Co.Ltd] and held that the claimants were entitled to Rs. 25,000/-as compensation.

entities.text:
Dr. Safia Bee Vs.
National Insurance Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of the petition, 21.12.2019, until the date of realisation was also ordered against the petitioners herein.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though they had specifically stated in the written statement that the claimants suffered no injuries, the same was not considered.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the respondents, I am not inclined to consider the said contention of the petitioners, as the Tribunal had clearly found that there was no evidence adduced on behalf of the petitioners in the case and, dealing with the injuries suffered, only a consolidated amount was ordered.

I do not find 2025:KER:94544 OP (MAC) NO.150 OF 2023 &
conn.
any ground to interfere with the common award in question.
Accordingly, these original petitions fail and are dismissed.
